title: Enterprise Fidelity & Stability Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Purpose:
Provide a repeatable, cross-team playbook for measuring, maintaining, and communicating model service fidelity and stability for enterprise customers. This document explains the metrics, instrumentation, SLO decomposition, detection rules, escalation ladder, and pre-QBR preparation steps used by Customer Success, SRE, and Product to ensure customer-facing SLAs and quality expectations are met.

Scope:
- Applies to production inference paths used by enterprise customers (hosted API + Dedicated).
- Covers telemetry for generation, embeddings, and reranking endpoints.
- Excludes internal research workloads and non-production staging clusters.

Definitions (quick):
- Fidelity: semantic correctness and stability of responses relative to a customer’s expected behavior / golden prompt set.
- Availability: percentage of requests returning successful (2xx) responses within latency SLO.
- Degradation window: contiguous period where fidelity or availability falls below thresholds for the same tenant.
- Guardrail failure: an automated safety check (e.g., toxic content filter or format validator) that rejected >= 0.5% of a tenant’s requests in a 1h window.

Key owners and contacts:
- Customer Success lead: Priya Natarajan (owner for customer comms and QBR agenda)
- Oncall SRE: eng-sre oncall (primary for infrastructure/latency incidents)
- Model Quality Lead: Diego Alvarez (owner for fidelity regressions and evals)
- Dedicated Deployment SME: Lina Patel (private/dedicated cutover and rollback)
- Slack channels: #cust-success-ops (customer comms), #sre-inference (infra), #model-quality

Fidelity and Stability Metrics (measured per-tenant and rolled up):
- Golden-prompt pass rate (GPR): percent of golden-prompts that produce expected label/format. Target: >= 97% weekly for enterprise tiers.
- Semantic drift score (SDS): normalized similarity delta vs. baseline embeddings on prompt-set. Target: SDS <= 0.06 (lower is better).
- Successful-response rate (SRR): 2xx responses within latency SLO. Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly.
- Median P95 latency (request-to-first-token): baseline depends on tier: hosted < 180ms median; dedicated < 120ms median.
- Guardrail reject rate (GRR): percent of responses failing guardrails. Threshold: < 0.3% over 1 hour.
- Cost-per-1000-tokens (CPT): used in QBRs to explain economics.

SLO decomposition (example mapping):
- Customer-facing SLA (contract): 99.9% availability and fidelity >= 95% across golden prompts.
- Internal SLOs: SRR >= 99.95% service-wide; GPR >= 97% per-tenant weekly; GRR <= 0.3% hourly.
- Error budget policy: for enterprise customers, a monthly error budget consumption > 20% triggers proactive review and proposed remediation plan; > 50% triggers formal escalation and potential credits.

Instrumentation & telemetry (how we measure):
1) Golden prompt harness: each enterprise onboarding includes a 100–300 prompt set run nightly. Results are stored in the fidelity index and surfaced to the QBR dashboard. CLI example to run locally if needed:

$ redwood-eval-run --tenant-id T-12345 --prompt-set /prompts/enterprise/handbook-core.json --output s3://redwood-evals/T-12345/

2) Production sampling: 0.1% of production requests are shadowed to the fidelity evaluation pipeline to compute SDS and GPR without adding latency.
3) Distributed tracing: spans created with tags: service=inference, model_version, tenant_id, route. Example Prometheus metrics exported: inference_requests_total, inference_latency_seconds_bucket{quantile,tenant}, guardrail_rejects_total.
4) Cost telemetry: token_count and computed CPT stored per-request in the billing stream and aggregated daily. Example SQL snippet to produce CPT by tenant:

SELECT tenant_id, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SUM(cost) as cost, (SUM(cost)/SUM(tokens))*1000 as cost_per_1000_tokens FROM billing.events WHERE date >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY tenant_id;

Detection rules & alerting (who gets paged):
- Alert: fidelity-regression-tenant (severity P2): triggered when tenant GPR < 90% for 30m AND SDS > 0.12. Pager to: model-quality oncall -> then customer-success for high-value tenants.
- Alert: availability-degradation (severity P1): SRR < 99.5% for 10m -> paged to eng-sre primary and infra-rotation.
- Alert: guardrail-spike (severity P2): GRR > 1.0% in 15m -> paged to model-quality and #cust-success-ops channel (no immediate page unless customer impact).
- Cost anomaly: CPT increases > 40% week-over-week -> routed to FinOps and Customer Success (email).

Runbook: first 30 minutes (triage cadence)
1) Responsible: first responder (SRE or Model Quality depending on alert).
2) Immediately collect:
   - Request traces for the window (tracing service link),
   - Golden-prompt nightly run report (S3 path),
   - Deployment history (k8s rollout events / model_version),
   - Recent config changes (routing rules, quantization profile changes).
3) Quick triage checklist (do this in parallel):
   - Is the issue isolated to a single tenant or global? (check tenant_id cardinality in alerts)
   - Has a model version rolled out in the last 2 hours? (kubectl rollout history / model-registry)
   - Are infra metrics (GPU memory pressure, OOMs, pod restarts) elevated?
   - Any network anomalies / cloud provider advisories? (status pages)
4) If fidelity regression and root cause not obvious in 30m -> escalate to Model Quality lead and prepare an immediate rollback to last known-good model variant (see rollback steps).

Escalation ladder (roles and SLAs):
- 0–15m: oncall SRE / first responder performs initial mitigation and informs #incident-ops.
- 15–45m: Model Quality joins if fidelity-related. Customer Success lead notified for enterprise tenants; initiate customer-safe message draft.
- 45–120m: Cross-functional war room (SRE, Model Quality, Dedicated SME, Customer Success) if issue persists or customer-impacting.
- >120m: Exec briefing and legal/compliance loop if the issue affects contractual SLA or PII exposure.

Rollback and safety actions (when to rollback):
- Rollback to previous model variant when GPR drops > 7 percentage points and manual checks confirm output regressions for golden prompts.
- For dedicated/private tenants, coordinate with Dedicated SME to schedule in-window rollback (can require tenant approval for private infra).
- Quick rollback steps (engineer-run):
  1. Identify last-known-good model_version: CURR_VER -> grep model_registry | tail -n 10
  2. Trigger rollout: redwood-deploy --model-version CURR_VER --target pool-<tenant-pool> --strategy immediate
  3. Verify: run 20 golden prompts against the tenant endpoint and confirm GPR >= 95%.

Customer Communication play (templates & timing):
- Initial acknowledgement: within 30 minutes for P1/P2 impacting an enterprise account. Include summary, impacted services, and expected next update window.
- Status cadence: every 60 minutes until remediation or formal rollback.
- Post-incident report: within 48 hours include timeline, root cause analysis, and mitigation plan. Use the Postmortem template and attach telemetry graphs.
- Template snippet (copy-pasteable):

Subject: Incident update — inference instability for <tenant_name>

Hi <Customer_POC>,

We are actively investigating an issue affecting model response quality for requests to <endpoint>. Our engineers have identified a regression in fidelity for a subset of requests and are performing a rollback to a previous model variant as an immediate mitigation. Next update: in 60 minutes.

Regards,
<Redwood CS lead>

Pre-QBR preparation checklist (quarterly operationalization):
1) 14 days before QBR: confirm nightly golden-prompt runs have completed and upload the pass/fail CSV to the QBR folder.
2) 7 days: generate cost delta report (CPT), P95 latency trends, guardrail spikes, and top-5 fidelity regression examples with annotated prompts.
3) 3 days: dry-run the QBR deck with the CS lead and Model Quality to ensure explanations are actionable.
4) QBR deck contents (minimum): executive summary, availability & fidelity SLO performance, cost per 1k tokens trends, open risk items and remediation plan, proposed model/config changes with expected economic impact.

Dashboard and queries to include in QBRs:
- Tenant fidelity timeline: GPR daily moving average + golden-prompt failure examples (link to table).
- Availability heatmap: SRR by region and model_version.
- Cost bridge: CPT delta and contributor breakdown (batching, quantization, model_size).
- Example PromQL for SRR drop detection:

sum(rate(inference_requests_total{tenant_id=\"T-12345\",status=~\"2..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total{tenant_id=\"T-12345\"}[5m])) < 0.995

Post-incident follow-ups and continuous improvement:
- All incidents that consume > 20% of an enterprise customer’s monthly error budget require a triage meeting including Customer Success, Model Quality, and SRE within 7 business days.
- Maintain a shared regression test set: add newly discovered problematic prompts to the tenant's golden set and tag with failure mode.
- Quarterly model audit: Model Quality to run a model-variant stress test (1000+ edge prompts) and produce a mitigation plan for any regressions.

Appendices:
A) Example golden-prompt CSV columns:
- prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_label, match_threshold, last_valid_model_version, last_run_timestamp

B) Escalation contact matrix (internal):
- model-quality-oncall: paged via PagerDuty (PD alias: pd-model-quality)
- eng-sre-oncall: pd-sre-primary
- customer-success-lead: email and slack @Priya Natarajan

C) Quick checklist for Dedicated tenants (network & infra specific):
1) Validate tenant peering: confirm all firewall rules and peering entries are present and no recent ACL changes.
2) If private deployment: check KMS logs for key rotation events in the last 24h.
3) For on-prem: confirm GPU driver versions and CUDA patch level are as expected (recommended: CUDA 12.2, driver >= 535.xx).

Document maintenance and versioning:
- Owner: Customer Success (Priya Natarajan). Review cadence: quarterly or after any P1 incident.
- Change log: note significant changes below (include PR and reviewer IDs).

Change log:

End of document.
